content: I was asked by some of the Iris-Lean people whether grw could be upstreamed from Mathlib to e.g. Batteries, so that it can be used in Iris-Lean. Would this be a reasonable move, and is batteries the right place for the gcongr and grw tactics?
What about just a standalone library? (Which, I think, Mathlib could require as well.)

(I think batteries is also a possibility, but my feeling is that grw is still being developed/updated, so perhaps it's best not to move it "upstream" yet. Maybe one day we'll have bandwidth for a unification of grw and Kyle's ideas for a more flexible simp/rw...!)

In such a case, who should be responsible for reviewing the code? There are indeed currently some developments going on in grw at the moment (#38318) that are under review by the mathlib maintainers/reviewers. Would it still be their responsibility to review it if it becomes a separate library?
Presumably not? Would we all be happy with that?
Can iris-lean vendor grw, i.e. make a copy of the mathlib code (and manually update regularly/whenever an important feature is merged)? That seems like a better solution for now.

We want to avoid vendoring it if possible. Our requirements are basically that A) we don't absorb a Mathlib dependency, B) grw is stable enough that our code doesn't become a maintenance problem and C) it has to be compatible with our typeclass hierarchy.

We will be working on C--we maintain an IrisMath project with both an Iris Lean and Mathlib dependency. However there's quite a big part of Iris which is painful to use without generalized rewriting (heaps, maps, and iterated separating conjunctions). In an ideal world, generalized rewriting would be tightly integrated plain Iris much more.

Understood! My understanding is that currently,

  • grw is still undergoing active changes,
  • moving grw to a separate repository would reviewing these changes (and adapting mathlib) harder --- so is a non-starter from mathlib's side,
  • Iris-Lib doesn't want to depend on mathlib,
  • a big part of Iris-Lib is more painful to use without grw

I don't see how to square this circle in the short term, without vendoring.

@Jovan Gerbscheid How large are breaking changes in the grw implementation expected to be? In other words, if grw is very stable in practice, then perhaps vendoring is not as much of a hazard as Markus fears?

In #38318, which adds the new grw implementation, only about 3 existing grw proofs in mathlib had to be adapted. So stability is not so much an issue there.

There might be more breaking changes if we want to align grw with the new rw that is being developed by the FRO. But in that case there will be equally breaking changes to rw, which will probably be a bigger worry than grw :).
Would it be possible to do these changes to grw as part of batteries instead of as part of mathlib? Or can only stable tactics be moved to batteries?
I'm curious, what's the main use case for this in Iris-Lean? Are these mainly equivalence relations that you want to rewrite with or something weaker?

There are a bunch of relations that one wants to rewrite with in Iris Lean. Some are equivalence relations (e.g. bi-entailment ⊣⊢), but not all are equivalence relations. The most important non-equivalence relation is the entailment of the logic P ⊢ Q. It is quite common that one wants to rewrite with entailments, but currently this is not possible, requiring more manual proofs.

The other broad class of use cases has to do with rewriting by equivalences ≡ or indexed equivalences ≡{n}≡ under non-expansive functions. All of our heap-based constructions are only up to equivalence or indexed equivalence, not equality, and currently there's a lot of annoying bookkeeping required to apply these rewriting lemmas by hand.

Markus de Medeiros said:

and currently there's a lot of annoying bookkeeping required to apply these rewriting lemmas by hand.

To illustrate the issue, consider Iris/BI/Updates.lean. We use .trans and *_mono theorems in place of generalized rewriting.

Michael Rothgang said:

  • moving grw to a separate repository would reviewing these changes (and adapting mathlib) harder --- so is a non-starter from mathlib's side,

I don't think this is obviously the case!

Why don't we just move grw to a separate repo? Jovan can work there uninterrupted, merging changes as he sees fit (or finding/appointing other maintainers there, and doing internal review with them). Mathlib will just bump the pinned dependency when he says we should. (The lean-release-managers team would need write access for emergency fixes on release days, but I don't anticipate this being a practical problem.)
